_readme: SAIRNroofing Phase 5 contingency-agreement rescission rule seed. OHIO ONLY,
matching the state already seeded for licensing in Phase 3a.
READ FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE -- codes.ohio.gov, the Revised Code itself, on
2026-08-25. Not a roofing-vendor summary and not a law-firm blog. Each rule
carries citation, URL, verbatim quote and read_on date, the same standard as
sairnroofing_certifications_seed_ohio.json.
── THE FINDING THAT SHAPES THIS FEATURE ─────────────────────────────────
OHIO HAS NO ROOFING-SPECIFIC CONTINGENCY STATUTE. Colorado (C.R.S. 6-22-101
et seq.) and Florida (Fla. Stat. 489.147) both wrote roofing-specific laws;
Ohio did not. What governs an Ohio storm-chase contract instead is the
GENERAL Home Solicitation Sales Act, R.C. 1345.21-.28 -- and it is arguably
stronger, because it is conditional on HOW the sale was solicited rather
than on what trade performed it.
That is the same shape as the Phase 3a Ohio finding, where the correct
answer was also a negative one (Ohio licenses no roofing trade). The danger
is identical too: an app that generalised 'Ohio's 3-day HSSA window' to
Colorado would be wrong about the trigger event, the unit AND the count.
So no state except Ohio is seeded, and the engine returns 'no_rule' -- an
honest empty state, explicitly NOT the same as 'no right of rescission'.
── THE TRAP: 'BUSINESS DAY' DOES NOT MEAN MONDAY-TO-FRIDAY HERE ─────────
R.C. 1345.21 defines a business day as 'any calendar day except Sunday, or
the following business holidays' and then names eleven. SATURDAY IS A
BUSINESS DAY IN OHIO. The first draft of api/_lib/roofing-agreements.js
excluded Saturday on the ordinary meaning and was wrong by a full day on
any Thursday or Friday signing. Because the statute enumerates its holidays,
they are applied exactly rather than disclosed as a gap.
── THE PART A CONTRACTOR WILL NOT KNOW ──────────────────────────────────
Under R.C. 1345.23 the seller must give BOTH a conspicuous written notice of
the right to cancel AND a separate, detachable, duplicate 'Notice of
Cancellation' form. Fail either and the buyer's right to cancel does not
expire -- it runs until the seller complies. A roofer missing the form has
open-ended exposure on every contract they ever signed, and no calendar
shows it. That is why indefinite_if_noncompliant is modelled as a real
status instead of being collapsed into an ordinary deadline.
── WHAT IS NOT IN THIS FILE, DELIBERATELY ───────────────────────────────
The verbatim NOTICE TEXT a contractor prints on the contract. The quotes
below are evidence for the RULE, cited to the section they came from. The
wording that goes on a real customer's contract is entered in-app with a
named source, per Michael's decision 2026-08-25 -- generated statutory
language that is close but not verbatim is worse than none.

data.authority: Ohio Rev. Code 1345.22 (Home Solicitation Sales Act -- right of buyer to cancel)
data.verbatim: You, the buyer, may cancel this transaction at any time prior to midnight of the third business day after the date of this transaction.
data.verbatim_source: R.C. 1345.23 -- the notice language the seller must place, clearly and conspicuously, in bold-face type of a minimum size of ten points, on the copy of the contract left with the buyer.
notes: This is the GENERAL home-solicitation statute, not a roofing statute. Ohio has no roofing-specific contingency law.

R.C. 1345.21 defines 'business day' as any calendar day EXCEPT SUNDAY and eleven named holidays: New Year's day, Martin Luther King day, Presidents' day, Memorial day, Juneteenth day, Independence day, Labor day, Columbus day, Veterans day, Thanksgiving day, Christmas day. Saturday counts.
The statute names those days and does not provide for observed-day shifting when one falls on a Sunday, so the engine applies none.
Refunds: the seller must return all payments within ten business days of receiving the cancellation notice (R.C. 1345.23). Not modelled as a deadline in v1 -- flagged, not faked.

data.authority: Ohio Rev. Code 1345.21(A) (definition of 'home solicitation sale')
data.verbatim: A sale of consumer goods or services in which the seller or a person acting for the seller engages in a personal solicitation of the sale at a residence of the buyer ... or in which the buyer's agreement or offer to purchase is made at a place other than the seller's place of business.
notes: Loaded as 'superseded' ON PURPOSE: this row is the SCOPE evidence for RFCON-OH-HSSA-CANCEL, not a second live rule. Only one active rule may govern a state, and two active rows would be exactly the ambiguity the engine flags.

The exclusion matters as much as the definition: the Act does not reach a sale where the buyer initiated contact and the seller has a fixed business establishment in Ohio where those goods or services are regularly offered. That is why signing_venue is captured at signature time and cannot be inferred later.

_why: Read on 2026-08-25 and recorded so the research is not lost, but NOT loaded.
A rule nobody has verified against the CURRENT statute text should not
render as a confident date on a contractor's screen. Seeding any of these
is a deliberate act with its own verification pass, not a copy-paste.

CO.note: Rescind within 72 hours after WRITTEN notice from the insurer that the claim is denied in whole or in part. C.R.S. 6-22-103 separately enumerates required contract terms and a bold hold-in-trust clause. The right does NOT extend to supplemental roofing services whose damage could not reasonably have been foreseen at the initial inspection -- which is this app's `asserted` / hidden_damage supplement class.

FL.note: Cancel within 10 days after execution or by the official start date, whichever comes first, where the contract arises from events under a Governor-declared state of emergency. Omitting the prohibited-practices notice can let the owner void the contract after ten days.

TX.authority: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 27.02; Tex. Ins. Code 4102.163
TX.note: NO rescission right in 27.02 -- it mandates a 12-point boldface notice that the insured must pay the deductible. Seeding TX as if it had a cancellation window would invent a right that does not exist. Ins. Code 4102.163 separately bars a roofing contractor from acting as, or advertising as, a public adjuster.
